:::{#exr-bernoulli-score-equation}
#### Solving the score equation of a binary sample

In the setting of @exr-bernoulli-score-sum, assume $\outbar \in (0, 1)$:
the [sample](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-sample) has at least one [event](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-event) and at least one non-event.
Solve the [score equation](#def-score-equation) $\score(\prob) = 0$ for $\prob \in (0, 1)$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-bernoulli-score-equation}

For $\prob \in (0, 1)$, $\precision = 1 / \paren{\prob(1 - \prob)}$ is finite and positive, <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
and $n > 0$, so $n \precision \neq 0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0 &= \score(\prob)
&& \text{(score equation)}\\
0 &= n \precision (\outbar - \prob)
&& \text{(score function of a binary sample)}\\
0 &= \outbar - \prob
&& \text{(divide both sides by $n \precision \neq 0$)}\\
\prob &= \outbar
&& \text{(add $\prob$ to both sides)}
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\outbar \in (0, 1)$, this solution lies in $(0, 1)$.

:::
